WENDLECOTE RESIDENTS' ASSOCIATION
Minutes of the Annual General Meeting held on Thursday 12 March 2026 at 19:30 in Wendlecote Village Hall

Present: 47 members (attendance sheet attached) and 3 guests, among them the ward councillor, Adaeze. In the chair: Gareth. Minutes: Priyanka (secretary).
Apologies: 11 members sent their apologies.

1. Welcome and quorum
The chair welcomed members and guests and thanked the hall committee for the use of the room. The constitution requires 30 members to be present for a general meeting to be quorate. With 47 members present, the meeting was declared quorate.

2. Minutes of the last annual general meeting
The minutes of the meeting held on 13 March 2025 were approved as a true record, proposed by Hamid and seconded by Ruth. There were no matters arising that were not already on the agenda.

3. Chair's report
Gareth summarised the year. The association ran the summer fair, which raised 2,140 for the hall roof fund, and organised two litter picks along the river path, each with more than twenty volunteers. The campaign for a pedestrian crossing on Mill Lane continued, and the council has now agreed to carry out a traffic survey in May. Membership rose from 212 to 236 households. He thanked the committee and the volunteers who deliver the newsletter to every house four times a year.

4. Treasurer's report
The outgoing treasurer, Colm, presented the accounts for the year. Income was 6,480: membership fees 2,832, the summer fair 2,140 and donations 1,508. Expenditure was 4,915, mostly newsletter printing (1,620), insurance (740), hall hire (600) and equipment for the river path clean-up (1,955). The year closed with a surplus of 1,565 and a bank balance of 9,310. The accounts had been checked by an independent examiner, who found no issues. Members approved the accounts by a show of hands, with no votes against.

5. Reports from the working groups
Environment group (Hannah): the group planted 150 native bulbs on the verge outside the school and repaired two of the four bird boxes on the green. It would like to survey the river path for invasive plants in the summer and is looking for two more volunteers.
Events group (Dominic): besides the summer fair, the group ran a quiz night in November that broke even. A film night in the hall is planned for April if a licence can be arranged at a reasonable price.
Roads and transport group (Hamid): apart from the crossing campaign, the group reported three damaged street lights and a blocked drain on Station Road to the council; two of the lights have been repaired.

6. Hall roof fund
Ruth reported for the hall committee that the roof repair has been quoted at 18,400. With the 2,140 from the summer fair, the fund now stands at 11,750. The committee has applied to two charitable trusts for the rest and expects their answers by the end of May. Work cannot start before September because bats roost in the roof space during the summer, and an ecologist will check the roof before any work begins. Members asked whether the association would cover any shortfall; Ruth said that the committee would come back to a general meeting before committing any of the association's money. One member offered to organise a sponsored walk for the fund in June, and several members volunteered to help.

7. Election of officers
Gareth agreed to stand again as chair and was re-elected unopposed. Priyanka was re-elected as secretary unopposed. Colm stood down as treasurer after six years. Two members were nominated for the post: Odette and Lewis. After short statements from both candidates, a secret ballot was held. Odette received 29 votes and Lewis 16, with 2 spoiled papers. Odette was declared elected as treasurer. The meeting thanked Colm warmly for his years of service.

8. Motion 1: bicycle racks on the village green
Proposed by Ines, seconded by Dominic: "That the association spends up to 1,200 from its reserves on four bicycle racks at the edge of the village green, subject to council permission." Ines explained that bicycles are currently chained to the railings, which damages the paint and blocks the footpath for pushchairs. One member asked whether the racks would attract theft; Ines replied that they would stand in view of the shop's camera. Vote: 31 for, 9 against, 7 abstentions. The motion was carried.

9. Motion 2: annual membership fee
Proposed by the committee: "That the annual fee rises from 12 to 15 per household from 1 April 2026." The treasurer-elect said that this year's surplus makes an increase unnecessary for now. Several members said that a higher fee would put off new households, especially in the new flats on Station Road. Vote: 18 for, 26 against, 3 abstentions. The motion was defeated, and the fee stays at 12.

10. Motion 3: community garden
Proposed by Kwame, seconded by Hannah: "That the association creates a community garden on the unused plot behind the hall." Members supported the idea in principle but asked who would look after the garden and whether the hall committee owns the plot. It was agreed to set up a working group of Kwame, Hannah and Lewis to report to the next general meeting. No vote was taken.

11. Any other business
(a) Speeding on Mill Lane: several members reported cars driving well above the limit at school times. The secretary will write to the council asking for the May survey to include speed data.
(b) Newsletter: volunteers are needed to deliver on the east side of the village.
(c) The ward councillor said that the council's grant scheme for community projects opens in June and that the garden might qualify.
(d) Recycling: the council will collect glass separately from July; the collection days will be printed in the next newsletter.
(e) Defibrillator: Hamid reported that the defibrillator outside the shop was checked in February and that its pads expire in October; the committee will order replacements.

12. Date of the next meeting
The next general meeting will be held in September; the date will be announced in the summer newsletter. The meeting closed at 21:10.
